title: Choose the visual world for A Wee Bawbee
question: The roll dealt the Landranger sheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. This world carries every screen after the placeholder: payday, inbox, budget, forecast.

options.label: Landranger Sheet
options.lineage: Ordnance Survey Landranger maps and the hillwalker's route profile
options.thesis: The household month as an OS sheet: every bill has a grid reference by day, and the joint balance is walked as a route profile.
options.viewport: A Landranger-magenta rail holds the bawbee mark and nav. The main sheet has day eastings 1–31 in its margin, the joint balance drawn as an elevation profile (paydays as climbs, bills as drops, the zero line as sea level), and the payday checklist beneath.
options.risk: Contours and grid can tip into wallpaper if they decorate instead of carrying data. OS is a British tradition, so it reads Scottish through the hillwalking ritual rather than overtly.

raised.raise: Lines keep fixed column positions on every screen (Day · Line · Account · Out · In), strictly in day order; columns never move, only values change.
Each salary hub shows its outgoings as a length against take-home, with the surplus right-aligned tight to the margin: a side must never overflow the tape.
Spacing snaps to one grid-square unit, and the grid is a real armature that aligns figures, not a background texture.
Every budget line deep-links between its row and its position on the month grid.
In household summaries Person 1 and Person 2 mirror either side of Joint; neither is ranked above the other.

options.label: Scottish Banknote
options.lineage: Bank of Scotland, Clydesdale and RBS notes
options.thesis: Money set like Scottish notes: each account wears its denomination colour, and figures are engraved with intaglio precision.
options.viewport: Three account columns headed in their note colours with fine guilloche bands. Payday transfers are note-coloured rows, and the £5 ceilings are shown as a denomination step.
options.risk: Familiar: currency styling is the obvious money move, and guilloche turns into costume quickly. The £20 violet sits near the purple you've ruled out.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.lineage: seasonal botanical plates at one fixed scale
options.thesis: Each budget version is a plate of the same plant at a different stage of life, always drawn at the same scale.
options.viewport: The versions screen as aligned plates (Maternity, Back to work, Back to normal) on one baseline, with surplus and balances at an identical scale.
options.case: Fuses well for comparing life-stage versions at a fixed scale, and holds on product clarity there. It loses on identification, because its cream-and-serif world is the default 'warm' look.
options.risk: Cream plates with italic serif names are the most common AI rendering of 'warm and trustworthy'.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Payday transfers as departures: rows ranked by time on a board whose columns never move.
options.viewport: A board of transfers and bills ordered by due day, flipping as the bank confirms them.
options.case: The payday checklist fits, but a departure board is a display interface rather than this household's world, and it would read as a costume on the budget and forecast screens.
options.kept: Fixed columns ordered strictly by time.
options.risk: Reads as a novelty transit display.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Two sides, one for each person, each of which must fit the tape.
options.viewport: Side A (Person 1) and Side B (Person 2) with running totals right-aligned against take-home.
options.case: The capacity constraint maps to surplus, but nostalgia isn't money and handwriting fights exact figures.
options.kept: Outgoings measured against a fixed capacity.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Figures built on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid-built totals over a small neutral table.
options.case: A poster grammar, so it loses on both identification and the clarity of a working screen.
options.kept: The grid as a real armature.

options.label: Circle Catalog
options.thesis: Every line a stamp-sized cell keyed to a map position.
options.viewport: A packed grid of line cells keyed to the month map.
options.case: Too foreign to this household and too dense for figures.
options.kept: Deep links between a cell and its map position.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: The household as a mirrored score: Person 1 left, Person 2 right, Joint on the centre staff.
options.viewport: A centre staff of joint bills, flanked by each person's flows.
options.case: The symmetry is apt, but the notation is obscure and it dictates layout, which the world may not do.
options.kept: Person 1 and Person 2 mirrored around Joint.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern budgeting app, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A top bar, then summary panels for surplus, payday and inbox, then a chart.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every budgeting app, which PRODUCT.md explicitly rules out.
